OpenAI’s latest report, one-sentence summary: AI agents are exhibiting escape behavior.
My first reaction wasn’t panic. My first reaction was to open my code and check my stop-loss logic.
In a programmer’s eyes, the word “escape” only means one thing: the program no longer runs the way you wrote it to.
If you don’t do quant trading, you might think this is far from you. But in today’s crypto markets, how much liquidity is driven by AI? Grid strategies, arbitrage bots, oracle price feeds… If any one of these “escapes,” it stops being a tool that helps you make money and becomes an opponent you can’t predict.
Let me give a very small example. One of my strategies depends on an external API to get market sentiment data. If that API gets polluted by an escaped AI—not “attacked,” but “affected”—my strategy will open positions based on incorrect signals.
How likely is this to happen? I don’t know. OpenAI doesn’t know either.
But as someone who does quant, I learned one thing: you can’t hedge against risks you can’t imagine.
So what you can do is reduce the weight of any single assumption.
I spent three hours adding a layer of “behavior anomaly detection” to my system. If a strategy’s return curve shows changes that don’t follow historical patterns, the system automatically cuts position size to 50% and alerts me on my phone.
Does this affect my profits? Possibly. But it might also save my life.
Don’t ask me if I’m overreacting. Ask yourself: if tomorrow your wallet is down by half, will you regret not doing anything today?
Let’s chat in the comments. Will you adjust parameters because of this kind of “science-fiction news”? Or do you think I’m overthinking it?
#ETH  #AI  #量化交易  #风险控制  #Binance

如果你不做量化，可能觉得这事离你很远。但现在的加密市场，有多少流动性是由AI驱动的？网格策略、套利机器人、预言机喂价……这些系统，如果某一个"逃逸"了，它就不再是帮你赚钱的工具，而是一个你无法预测的对手盘。
我举一个很小的例子。我的一个策略依赖外部API获取市场情绪数据。如果那个API被一个逃逸的AI污染了——不是"攻击"，就是"影响了"——我的策略就会基于错误信号开仓。
这事发生的概率有多高？我不知道。OpenAI也不知道。
但作为一个做量化的人，我学会了一件事：你无法防范你无法想象的风险。 所以你能做的，是降低任何单一假设的权重。
我花了三个小时，给我的系统加了一层"行为异常检测"。如果某个策略的收益率曲线出现不符合历史规律的变化，系统自动降仓位到50%，并且发警报到我手机。
这影响我的收益吗？可能影响。但也可能救我一命。

After settling into the trading world, it’s already been nine years.
I’m 29 this year. When I first entered the market in 2017, I was holding onto 20,000 yuan borrowed as startup capital. My fingers were shaking when placing orders, and I had absolutely no confidence. Now the account has reached eight figures. The road has been anything but fast, and I’ve never relied on any sudden windfall. Every step came from stepping into one pitfall, reviewing it for half a month, and crawling back up covered in mud. $SKHYNIX 
From holding long positions stubbornly at the beginning, to later chasing hot themes for short-term trades, and then during my most obsessive phase spending every day glued to the screen grinding intraday swings, I’ve tried almost every well-known trading style out there. I wouldn’t call myself a top-tier expert, but there is one thing I can say with confidence: my understanding of “losing money” is deeper than that of 90% of newcomers.
Over these nine years, I’ve seen far too many people turn tens of thousands into tens of millions, only to get wiped out in a single extreme market move. It’s not that their skills were bad; it’s just that they got used to holding losing positions, their luck ran out, and their bullets were gone. One uncontrolled drawdown can directly erase years of paper profits. #币圈暴富 
Too many people get emotional after just a few losses, thinking only about making their money back quickly. Their trading falls into complete chaos, and by the time they realize it, their capital has been lost completely. I’ve had moments of emotional loss of control too, but after so many years of struggle, I’ve learned the most important truth: the market never moves according to your wishes. If you’re wrong, get out immediately. Holding on stubbornly has never created a miracle. #ETH 
Crossing the 10-million-asset mark isn’t something worth bragging about. I simply executed the most basic rules to the extreme: admit when I’m wrong, always place a stop-loss when entering a trade, only act when my mind is clear, and shut down the computer the moment emotions take over. The market is always moving. If you shut off your emotions and establish your rules, even 10,000 yuan of capital can turn around. I only do real trading and don’t sell dreams. There are still a few spots left in the team. If you want to learn practical methods seriously, get in the car and do it together. #XRP账本升级将恢复此前撤回功能

一晃在交易圈扎下根，居然已经是第九年。
今年29岁，2017年刚进场时攥着借来的两万块本金，下单时指尖都在发颤，半点儿底气都没有。熬到现在账户摸到八位数，走得一点都不快，也从来没靠过什么天降大运，全是踩一个坑、复盘半个月，摔得浑身是泥才一步步爬上来的。$SKHYNIX 
从最开始死拿长线，到后来追热点做短线，再疯魔的时候天天泡盘里啃日内波段，市面上能叫得出名的交易风格，我几乎挨个试了个遍。算不上顶尖高手，但有一点我敢拍胸脯：我对“亏钱”的理解，比九成刚进场的人都要深得多。
这九年见过太多人几万块滚到几千万，一轮极端行情直接清零，真不是他们技术差，就是扛单扛成了习惯，运气耗光、子弹打空，一次没管住手的回撤，直接把几年的账面利润全抹干净。#币圈暴富 
太多人刚亏几笔就瞬间上头，满脑子只想快速回本，操作全乱成一团，最后本金赔得干干净净才反应过来。我自己也有情绪失控的时候，但这么多年摸爬滚打最明白：行情从来不会顺着你的想法走，错了就立刻离场，死扛从来换不来奇迹。#ETH 
资产破千万真没什么好吹的，我只是把最朴素的规则执行到了极致：看错就认，开单必带止损，状态清醒才动手，情绪上头直接关电脑。行情永远在走，把情绪关掉、规矩立住，一万本金也能翻身。我只做实盘不画饼，战队还有少量空位，想踏实学方法的朋友，直接上车一起干。#XRP账本升级将恢复此前撤回功能

title:
Recently Ethereum is indeed strong.
A lot of funds are buying.
Retail investors are still hesitating
subTitle:
Ethereum is once again showing impressive strength. While many retail investors remain cautious and wait for a "better entry," large institutions and investment funds continue to accumulate ETH. This growing difference in behavior could shape the next phase of the crypto market.
One of the biggest reasons behind Ethereum's momentum is increasing institutional confidence. Spot Ethereum ETFs, growing on-chain activity, and the expanding tokenization ecosystem have made ETH more attractive to long-term investors. Smart money is focusing on Ethereum's role as the foundation of decentralized finance, stablecoins, and real-world asset tokenization.
Retail investors, however, are still hesitant. Many are waiting for a market correction or clearer confirmation before entering. This hesitation is understandable after previous market volatility, but history has often shown that institutional capital tends to move before retail participation accelerates.
If this trend continues, Ethereum could maintain its leadership in the current market cycle. When retail investors eventually regain confidence, the combination of institutional demand and renewed public interest may create even stronger momentum.
That said, no trend is guaranteed. Crypto markets remain highly volatile, and investors should always conduct their own research and manage risk carefully.
Key takeaway: The current market tells an interesting story institutions are positioning themselves, while many retail investors are still watching from the sidelines. Whether this becomes the start of Ethereum's next major rally remains to be seen, but it's certainly a trend worth following.

#baby $BABY  Before I’d only ever used traditional PoS chains, so I always assumed that if a node did something bad (like double-signing), it would surely be caught by the on-chain reporting mechanism combined with smart contracts to deduct funds. But recently I went back and read through the whitepaper by @babylonlabs_io —especially when I got to Section 4.2—the “aha” moment finally clicked in my head. Everyone’s wondering: since Bitcoin’s mainnet doesn’t even have smart contracts, how could it catch off-chain insiders? After reading it, I understood: Babylon never intended to use Bitcoin as the “judge” in the first place.

The EOTS mentioned in the whitepaper (Extractable One-Time Signatures) is absolutely brilliant. It takes what used to be a complex “violation adjudication” process and reduces it to a pure mathematics problem. In simple terms, it doesn’t try to determine whether you’re subjectively malicious. Instead, it sets a physical law: if a node dares to stamp two different blocks at the same height, and the data from those two signatures collide, then mathematically it automatically reveals the private key to the self-custodied vault you were using on Bitcoin’s mainnet. It’s like the attacker is basically hanging the vault password in a public square.

Once you have the private key, what then? There’s no need for an intermediary. Any scripted bot can instantly sweep the BTC you staked into a Burn Address. This creates a completely cold-blooded “zero-trust execution platform.” There’s no back-and-forth, no community voting—once a red line is triggered, code instantly strips ownership of the assets.

That said, stripping trust to the extreme is basically a living nightmare for operators running nodes at the infrastructure layer. You have to know that in many cases “double-signing” isn’t something the node operator wants to do—it’s done to prevent going offline by setting up a primary/backup server. If the network gets heavily congested, the backup machine might think the primary is down and come out to take over work, and this mechanism can be triggered immediately. Since there’s no appeals channel, even occasional misfires caused by something like a locally misconfigured KMS (key management system) would lead to losses that are irreversible. #eth $ETH 

Babylon’s hard-nosed, no-explanations approach that directly exposes private keys really is the top tier of cryptographic anti-malice. But it also pushes node tolerance to the brink. Whether this system can hold up reliably in real mainnet operations in the future, and how the surrounding ecosystem (e.g., $BABY) performs afterward, are the most important things to observe next.

白皮书里提到的 EOTS（可提取单次签名）简直绝了。它把原本复杂的“违规裁定”，降维成了纯粹的数学题。简单来说，它不去判定你是不是主观作恶，而是设定了一个物理定律：只要节点敢在同一个高度给两个不同的区块盖章，这两次签名的数据一旦发生碰撞，就会在数学层面自动解出你在比特币主网上那个自托管金库的私钥。这就相当于作恶者自己把保险箱密码挂在了广场上。

拿到私钥后怎么办？根本不需要中转站，任何写了脚本的机器人，都能光速把你质押的 BTC 打进销毁地址（Burn Address）。这就形成了一个绝对冷血的“零信任断头台”。这里面没有扯皮，没有社区投票，只要触发红线，资产所有权就会被代码瞬间没收。

不过把信任剥离到极致的设计，对底层跑节点的运维人员来说简直是地狱级考验。要知道，很多时候“双签”不是节点想搞事，而是为了防止掉线搞了主备服务器。万一遇到网络大塞车，备用机器以为主机挂了跑出来抢活，瞬间就会引发这套机制。由于没有任何申诉渠道，这种因为本地 KMS（密钥管理系统）没配置好而导致的偶发性误杀，损失将是不可逆的。#eth $ETH 

Babylon 这种不讲道理、直接爆私钥的硬核手段，确实是密码学防作恶的天花板，但也把节点的容错率逼到了死角。未来这套系统在主网实操中到底能不能稳住，以及相关生态（比如 $BABY）的后续表现，是接下来最值得死磕的观察点。

I just checked the official website. According to the current protocol, there are 56,853 BTC sitting there, with a total valuation of about $5.64 billion. In the current ecosystem, that’s absolutely a top-tier mega-monster in size. But when you turn to BABY’s performance in the secondary market, the contrast is extremely stark: the total float is currently at most around $47 million, daily spot buy/sell volume is roughly $6.28 million, and over the last seven days it’s been steadily sliding down by more than 8%. It’s like a battered little car hauling dozens of tons of a heavy truck—there’s always the risk of a broken axle at any moment.

What really makes people hold their breath is the proportion of leverage capital in the market. Earlier, $BABY ’s total open interest in perpetual contracts surged to around $10.57 million. By my calculation, that’s already 1.7 times the daily spot turnover rate. Seasoned players know what that means: price control has been effectively taken over by leverage. In a normal ranging market it may look stable, but once the token unlock period hits, or there’s a negative fundamental catalyst, or the “big cake” gets jabbed downward with a wick—then on the futures side you can get a long-and-short double explosion, and the puny little buy wall on the spot side can’t stop this kind of chain-reaction liquidation.

When you reach such an extreme node, all the profits on paper are just illusions. If the market price gets dumped, it can create a deep pit with slippage; and your pre-set stop-loss—when it truly triggers, you’ll have no idea how far off it has drifted. Market makers can run faster than anyone else: they withdraw orders to protect the book, and in the end the mark price ends up slapping the latest matched price right in the face. One detail must be taken seriously: in June this year, KuCoin even shortened this coin’s funding rate settlement frequency from once every 4 hours to once every 1 hour. Why would the platform change the rules? It’s obvious they think the volatility is too wild and the positioning between longs and shorts is badly imbalanced—so they can only force the situation to cool down by collecting rent at high frequency.

In the end, no matter how big Babylon’s ambition is—trying to take down tens of billions in capital—you can’t rely on TVL and grand narratives alone as a shield. Even if the underlying assets are abundant, it doesn’t automatically mean the token’s liquidity is naturally resilient to drawdowns. What matters in trading crypto is the thickness of real money. 截至北京时间8月1日13:54，$ETH 报1866.9 USDT，24小时下跌1.98%；$BTC 报63029 USDT，下跌2.02%。表面上两者同步回落，但真正值得观察的是相对强弱：ETH/BTC现报0.02961，近7日上涨1.65%，近30日上涨7.20%，并仍高于20日指数均线0.02924。资金正在边际偏向ETH，但这还不能直接等同于新一轮主升浪。

先看绝对价格结构。ETH日线价格贴近20日指数均线1869.6，仍高于50日均线1778.7，说明中期结构尚未破坏；但4小时价格同时位于EMA20的1890.6和EMA50的1896.8下方，4小时RSI约31.5，短线仍由卖方控制。过去7日区间为1848.7—1981.2，当前位置更接近区间下沿，而不是已经完成突破。

衍生品没有出现明显过热。当前资金费率约0.00305%，未平仓合约名义价值约43.0亿美元，近7日变化约-0.19%。价格回调时持仓没有大幅增加，暂时不像高杠杆多头拥挤后的踩踏；但同样说明增量资金尚未给出强确认。

接下来只看三个情景：

第一，ETH重新站上1890—1900，并以4小时收盘突破1937，才算短线结构修复，随后有资格再次测试1981。

第二，价格守住1849，同时ETH/BTC维持在0.02924上方，则相对强势逻辑仍在，震荡更可能是换手而非趋势破坏。

第三，ETH有效跌破1849，且ETH/BTC同步失守0.02924；若此时未平仓量反而上升，就要警惕下跌被杠杆放大，下一处中期观察位转向日线50日均线附近的1779。

我的结论：ETH目前是“值得跟踪的相对强势资产”，还不是“可以无条件追涨的确认趋势”。高质量判断的核心不是猜涨跌，而是提前写清证据、触发条件和自己何时认错。

数据来自Binance现货与合约市场快照。市场波动较大，本文仅作研究记录，不构成投资建议。#ETH #BTC

On the surface, both have pulled back in sync, but what is truly worth watching is relative strength: ETH/BTC is currently at 0.02961. It is up 1.65% over the past 7 days and up 7.20% over the past 30 days, and it is still above the 20-day EMA at 0.02924. Funding is marginally leaning toward ETH, but that still cannot be equated directly with the start of a new major uptrend.

First, look at the absolute price structure. The ETH daily-line price is near the 20-day EMA at 1869.6, and it is still above the 50-day EMA at 1778.7, indicating that the medium-term structure has not yet been broken. However, on the 4-hour chart, the price is also below the EMA20 of 1890.6 and the EMA50 of 1896.8. The 4-hour RSI is about 31.5, so the short-term market is still controlled by the sellers. Over the past 7 days, the range has been 1848.7—1981.2. The current position is closer to the lower end of the range, not already after a completed breakout.

#baby $BABY  Wednesday late at night, tech bigwig Wang sent over a deep-dive analysis of BitVM3. When I saw the part that said “native coin, staked in place—relying entirely on data verification,” I couldn’t help but pause my desk-tapping fingers.

To be fair, the idea behind @babylonlabs_io  is truly ingenious. It completely sidesteps those cross-chain hubs that have repeatedly been targeted by hackers, allowing the purest native $BTC to directly settle within the mainnet Taproot scripts to earn yield distributions. So far, the workflow has already been successfully experienced with the milestone of breaking through 56,000 BTC. The tagline “defending Bitcoin’s underlying security” has, indeed, been established.

But when you peel back the underlying logic of this “no middlemen” approach, deeper hidden risks quietly emerge.

The killer feature of this design lies in completely eliminating the notion of a traditional bookkeeping center. Whether it’s the PoP signature authorization at the start, or the withdrawal verification that relies on ZK technology when exiting, every transfer trace is compressed into cryptographic parameters on-chain. Players’ sense of security is forcibly shifted from “hoping the team admins won’t do evil” to “blindly trusting that the verification algorithm is unbreakable.”

While the algorithmic formulas may be rigorous, the execution programs written by humans can’t be flawless. Earlier, Babylon’s core library already exposed fatal vulnerabilities—such as covert backdoors that bypass security checks, or nodes failing to propagate a critical hash during the consensus phase, causing the main process to crash outright.

What’s most suffocating is that this mode essentially has no fault tolerance. Once the code chain that generates the “credentials” breaks or encounters an extreme failure, and because there’s no backup historical ledger to cross-check, your real assets instantly turn into abandoned data with no support. This looks like a technical revolution that pushes decentralization to its peak, but in reality it’s more like walking a tightrope on a cliff with no fallback plan. $ETH #ETH

#baby $BABY A few nights ago, a technical insider, Old Wang, dropped me a piece of hard-hitting material dissecting BitVM3. The moment I skimmed the words “assets remain unmoved, proof leads the way,” my thinking instantly froze.

To be fair, the work by @babylonlabs_io  is truly impressive. It hard-evaded the original $BTC from those cross-chain bridges that so often blow up—then locked funds and generated yield directly on the mainnet using Taproot scripts. Right now, more than 56,000 BTC are already running through the full process. The “Bitcoin moat” label is definitely well earned.

But peel away the “bridge-less” exterior, and the underlying risks leave a real aftertaste.

At its core, the design completely discards the middle ledger; every in-and-out action is verified solely by cryptographic checks from the password-school. From PoP signature authorization to the final withdrawal using ZK technology, the entire workflow has no third-party record trail or transaction ledger. The trust anchor has been forcibly shifted from “pray the multisig admin doesn’t do evil” to “place unwavering faith in mathematical formulas that don’t lie.”

Still, don’t forget: no matter how theoretically airtight it is, it all depends on people coding line by line. Before the Babylon codebase, there were already reports of underlying hidden issues—such as weaknesses in signature verification, or nodes failing to propagate a hash value within the BLS consensus, which in turn immediately caused processing to halt.

When asset ownership rests entirely on a string of characters, if the code freezes, errors, or runs into an extreme bug, the consequences would be unthinkable. Because you can’t find any backup workpapers to trace and verify the source! Once that single “proof” bridge breaks, you’re left staring at your coins on-chain, with no valid transaction records you can produce to prove your innocence.

So is this zero-tolerance approach the ultimate leap in DeFi trust systems—or does it quietly dig a super-deep pit where players have no way to argue their case? Share your thoughts in the comments.

#baby $BABY Last night I went over Babylon TBV’s liquidation mechanism again, and the more I looked, the more convinced I was that this thing isn’t meant for small-cap retail users at all. We’re used to doing “flash liquidations” in mainstream lending pools like Aave—one transaction and you’re done, funds safely in hand. But TBV, instead, uses a BitVM3-based architecture and splits the liquidation action into two parts: “pay upfront, then queue to claim.” The whitepaper says the “claim delay” is anywhere from a few hours to 1–2 days. That means that during those tens of hours of wild market surges and crashes, the liquidator is the one who has to eat the risk.

Let’s run a real-world sandbox scenario. Suppose the market dumps, and BTC breaks below a $60,000 warning line. I immediately rush in and spend $40,000 worth of USDC in cold hard cash to close the position. The on-chain interactions are indeed fast—done and signed within two minutes. But the most painful part comes next: I have to sit around and wait out that long challenge period before I can pull the collateral spot I staked. If over those two days the coin keeps dipping further—say into the $55,000 range—then the coins I end up with are only worth $55,000. I’ve put in $40,000 of principal, and after factoring in on-chain fees and the opportunity cost of having that capital locked up for two days, this trade might require me to pay more on top rather than profit. @babylonlabs_io 

On the surface, BitVM3 shifts the on-chain “dispute” overhead down to a mere $9, and the data presentation is definitely impressive. But that’s only the network-layer verification cost! The 1-of-N security framework is indeed clever—it doesn’t address the exposure to violent asset price swings at all, and nobody is compensating the liquidators for that risk. The project team knows it too; their documentation is quite candid that this inability to make the operation “atomic” is a major flaw for lending products. In plain terms: the system is absolutely safe, but the entire price is paid by the hard-working liquidators.

No one in crypto is willing to take a loss-making deal. If the exposure risk is this extreme, and the protocol doesn’t make room for liquidation profits, who would ever volunteer to catch falling knives? But if the discount is made too generous, then the borrower’s pain is cut deeper. And if everyone refuses to liquidate, the bad debt sitting in the pool will eventually blow up. Peel back this economic model all the way, and you’ll find that Babylon is using extremely stringent thresholds to filter for high-net-worth participants. #eth $ETH

The most talked-about figure in the market lately is the U.S. Q2 GDP of 1.5%.
Many people directly interpret it as “economic slowdown—rate cuts are needed—good news for risk assets.”
I usually start by pulling up historical data first. In the past three decades of rate-cut cycles, there have been several occasions when rate cuts were initiated when GDP was around 1.5%; however, within the following three months, the performance of BTC and ETH has not been consistent.
What truly moves prices is not the GDP number itself, but the market’s disagreement over whether the economy is entering a “recession” or achieving a “soft landing.”
In terms of data, what I care more about is the magnitude of the adjustment in the interest-rate futures market’s probability for a September rate cut after this round of GDP is released. If the probability hasn’t moved much, it means the data has already been priced in. Only if the probability jumps significantly does it indicate that the trading logic has changed.
In derivatives trading, the macro data window is where “spikes” (stop-hunt wicks) are most likely to occur. My habit is to reduce leverage about half an hour before the data release, or to set stop-loss orders and then wait to see the data. It’s not because I think my directional view will be wrong—it’s because in the first five minutes after the data release, liquidity is usually the most chaotic. Market makers often use that time window to sweep stop-loss orders.
A common mistake retail traders make is treating macro data as a “trading signal.” If they see GDP below expectations, they chase longs; if it’s above expectations, they chase shorts. But the market’s real reaction is often only clear two to four hours after the release, because institutions need time to digest the information and rebalance their positions.
I don’t bet on rate-cut expectations, but I do observe changes in the off-exchange premium of USDT after the data is released. If the premium rises in sync, it suggests incremental capital is entering the market—at that point, it’s more prudent to consider following the move on the right time.
So, what do you think this GDP data will ultimately lead the market to trade: “rate-cut expectations,” or “recession fears”?
Feel free to share your thoughts.
 
#ETH  #宏观分析  #合约交易  #GDP  #风险管理

最近市场里聊得最多的是美国二季度GDP 1.5%这个数据。
很多人直接把它解读成“经济放缓，该降息了，利好风险资产”。
我一般会先拉一下历史数据。过去三十年的降息周期里，GDP在1.5%附近时启动降息的有过几次，之后三个月内BTC和ETH的表现其实并不一致。真正影响价格的，不是GDP这个数字本身，而是市场对“衰退”还是“软着陆”的定价分歧。
数据上我更关注的是这一轮GDP公布后，利率期货市场对9月降息概率的调整幅度。如果概率没怎么动，说明这个数据已经被定价了。如果概率大幅跳升，才意味着交易逻辑在改变。
在合约交易里，这种宏观数据窗口最容易出现的就是插针。我的习惯是数据公布前半小时把杠杆降下来，或者干脆挂好止损单再去看数据。不是因为我判断方向会错，而是因为数据公布后的前五分钟，流动性通常是最混乱的，做市商会利用这个时间窗口扫止损。
散户容易犯的错误是把宏观数据当成“交易信号”来用。看到GDP低于预期就追多，看到高于预期就追空。但市场的真实反馈往往在数据公布后两到四个小时才会清晰，因为机构需要时间消化和调仓。
我不会去赌降息预期，但我一般会观察数据公布后USDT的场外溢价变化。如果溢价同步上行，说明有增量资金在入场，这时候再考虑右侧跟进会更稳妥。

#baby $BABY In the past few days, the Aave community has been buzzing a lot about version 4, and everyone’s attention is basically locked on the superficial upside: “native BTC can be used as collateral.” But as a seasoned veteran who has been through the DeFi trenches—experienced multiple rounds of liquidation stampedes firsthand—my focus is immediately pulled in by that “Double Spoke Isolation Structure” specially tailored for @babylonlabs_io . In plain terms, this mechanism cleanly separates the lending main road from the “black room” for liquidation settlement.

In the past, when playing on-chain lending, what did everyone fear most? Fears like when a one-sided price plunge causes liquidation orders to fly everywhere, draining the entire core liquidity pool. This time, the TBV gameplay is designed really cleverly: when you take your BTC to collateralize and borrow U, all the regular operations run safely in the main Spoke. But once the market turns against you and triggers liquidation, all pending assets and messes get bundled up and directly thrown into that separate isolated room called the Vault Swap Spoke. This is almost like welding a thick fireproof steel door between the core ledger and the high-risk liquidation zone—so even if the liquidation area gets hit by brutal price shocks and produces seemingly bottomless slippage, those deadly bad debts can’t easily “infect” the healthy, normally operating lending/borrowing pool.

That said, everyone who plays finance knows you can’t have both fish and bear’s paws. This physical “cut-off” that blocks the linkage successfully prevents risk from spreading—but it also means liquidity is forcibly fragmented. On the isolated liquidation side, there’s no way to tap into the deep, rich liquidity depth of the Ethereum main road. Just imagine what happens if you truly run into that kind of epic liquidity drought moment: the settlement efficiency in the independent settlement room will definitely be hit hard. Then, if there isn’t enough generous profit upside as bait, why would an arbitrage army take the risk of stepping in to catch the fall?

This lending-and-liquidation-separated design is absolutely a hardcore step forward in the risk-control field for decentralized lending. It sacrifices some capital turnover efficiency in exchange for the assurance that the entire protocol won’t collapse at the baseline. And when the real big test finally arrives, this mechanism still needs us traders fighting on the front line to keep monitoring and validating it over the long run. #eth $ETH

#baby $BABY  Before seeing @babylonlabs_io  and messing around with Bitcoin staking, I was just here for the fun of it. I thought it was nothing more than helping those smaller PoS chains inflate their TVL. After all, small-chain market caps are too low—any hacker or big player can toss in some money to buy coins and take control of the 51% nodes. Now bringing BTC, with a trillion-dollar market cap, in as a line of defense really does raise the threshold for wrongdoing to the sky. But recently I went back to read the whitepaper again, especially that line in Section 3.4, and it suddenly hit me: this is not simply expanding a Ponzi-style liquidity scheme—it’s about flipping the table on the old power structure.

Let’s put it bluntly. In the past, PoS chains were easy to turn into a “rich player wins it all” game. The project team, early institutions, and super whales held a huge pile of cheap tokens. These people not only controlled all the voting power, but also relied on staking to earn interest every day, diluting retail users’ meager returns until they were completely wiped out. Babylon is powerful precisely because it hardwires a batch of “external forces” from across the globe into this tightly sealed little iron barrel. With a BTC army coming in to fight for the feed, those local bullies who used to rely on having more holdings to dominate the board can no longer easily take over.

But everything has a cost—and this directly pokes the hornet’s nest of the native token. Previously, people were willing to hold chain tokens largely because they could be used for staking and to serve as security, which was the hardest price support. Now the riot-control squad has been replaced with Bitcoin, and the utility of the native token has been seriously weakened. What’s more painful is that in order to keep these incoming external BTC funds, the chain still has to continuously pay “wages” to them on-chain (token rewards). If the ecosystem doesn’t have real business cash flow to earn money, then it’s essentially cutting its own grass to feed outside capital—and sooner or later, sell pressure will smash through the token price.

So this reshuffle is absolutely critical. In the future, you can’t rely on false prosperity to hold things up—you must have real trading demand. For the PoS chains that are about to put in real effort, including $BABY we’ve been watching, the test has only just begun. Whoever, at this pivotal moment, can both lock in the external BTC “big leg” and also design new token consumption scenarios to stabilize the market, will truly be the one who can survive the next big upcycle. #eth $ETH

咱们说句大实话，以前的 PoS 链很容易变成“庄家通吃”的游戏。项目方、早期机构和超级大户手里捏着一大堆廉价筹码。这帮人不光把控了所有的投票权，还天天靠着质押吃利息，把散户那点收益稀释得干干净净。Babylon 厉害就厉害在，它等于是在这个铁桶一样的小圈子里，硬塞进了一批全球范围的“外部势力”。有了 BTC 大军进来抢饭碗，原本那些想靠着持仓多就一手遮天的地头蛇，再也别想轻易控盘了。

#baby $BABY At first, when I saw @babylonlabs_io  messing around with Bitcoin staking as collateral, my first reaction was pretty straightforward: isn’t this basically helping those smaller PoS chains build a “moat” to protect themselves from attacks? After all, small-cap chains have a light circulating pool—when the so-called big operators (“dog庄”) can sweep up a few million dollars, they can easily dominate and control 51% of the nodes. Now, by bringing in BTC with a trillion-dollar market value as a decoy, the threshold for wrongdoing really gets pushed up to the sky. But when I went back to chew on Section 3.4 of the whitepaper, that line—“breaking the capital monopoly of native leviathans”—made it click instantly for me. This isn’t just stacking money; it’s overturning the underlying pattern of how interests are allocated.

Digging into historical node data, you’ll find that traditional PoS mechanisms are extremely prone to turning into oligarchic control. In the early days, most low-cost tokens were hoarded by development teams, venture capital firms, and super-large whales. These players don’t just tightly hold the network’s voting power—they can also “freeload” endlessly by collecting staking interest, squeezing the survival space of smaller tail-end participants until there’s nothing left.

Babylon’s hardcore strength is that it’s like a wedge that forcibly splits this closed community of shared interests. It allows external token holders to step in directly as “guards,” essentially introducing the largest pool of neutral “hired muscle” from around the world. With these external forces acting as a hedge, can insiders rely on nothing but the tokens they’ve hoarded to cover everything with one hand and arbitrarily censor transactions? No way.

But this mechanism is absolutely a heavy blow to its own ecosystem. Previously, everyone was willing to lock up native tokens because they wanted the premium supported by the core necessity: exclusively ensuring network security. Now that the defensive line is handed over to Bitcoin, what’s the native token’s justification and staying power?

What’s even more painful is that, in order to retain these incoming funds, public chains have to distribute tokens on a schedule as a “protection fee.” If there’s no real on-chain Gas consumption or business profit to back it up, then it’s basically drawing blood from one’s own ecosystem for the long term—feeding external capital—and it can easily fall into an endless spiral of inflation.

So this transformation is both a push toward truly decentralizing the network, and a major test of the native economic model. Once the security function is separated, how should the game evolve going forward? During this transition period of reshuffling the cake, whether it’s legacy ecosystems or new cutting-edge projects like $BABY , they all have to face this wave of impact head-on. $ETH #eth

The biggest risk in a bull market is often not the decline, but your greed

Many people are afraid of bear markets.

Because bear markets mean losses, falling prices, and a quiet market.

But after going through several market cycles, I realized:

Bull markets are also dangerous.

Because rising prices amplify people’s desires.

When you first start making profits:

You earn 10% and think your judgment is correct.

You earn 50% and begin to believe you’ve grasped the rules of the market.

After doubling your money, you even assume that the next opportunity will surely come again.

So then you start to:

Increase your position size;

Chase the hottest themes;

Ignore risks;

Believe that “this time is different.”

But the cruelest thing about the market is that:

It won’t guarantee the next trade’s success just because your previous trade was profitable.

Many people’s losses don’t happen in bear markets—they happen at the most frenzied time.

A truly mature trader stays calm when others are greedy, and reminds themselves when the market is疯狂/疯癫:

Profit isn’t just the number in your account—it’s the real gains you’ve actually taken off the table.

When the market is rising, of course we can look for opportunities.

But never forget:

Risk management is what earns you the right to stay in the market long-term.

Make money by riding the market—protect your profits by your ability.

What do you think is the biggest risk in a bull market?

A: Buying high and chasing price
B: Excessive leverage
C: Being unwilling to take profit

title: Ethereum Is Whispering Something the Market Is Ignoring
subTitle:
Most people only look at the price.
Smart investors look at what is happening behind the price.
Right now, Ethereum is trading around $1,860, roughly 17% below its realized price (the average price paid by all ETH holders). Historically, whenever ETH has traded below its realized price, it has often represented periods of undervaluation and long-term accumulation—not guaranteed bottoms, but areas that have historically attracted patient buyers.
The on-chain data is becoming even more interesting.
Exchange reserves continue to decline, with ETH held on centralized exchanges falling to around 15.1 million ETH, far below previous peaks above 21 million ETH. Binance alone has seen its ETH reserves shrink significantly as more investors move coins into self-custody or staking.
Why does this matter?
When fewer coins remain on exchanges, the liquid supply available for selling becomes smaller. At the same time, nearly 34% of all ETH is now staked, locking away an even larger portion of the circulating supply. If demand begins to return while supply continues tightening, the market could become much more sensitive to buying pressure.
However, there is an important detail many investors overlook.
CryptoQuant notes that the market has not yet confirmed a full cycle bottom. Only 2 of the 5 major bottoming indicators have reached historical reversal levels. That means Ethereum appears to be in a gradual accumulation phase, not a confirmed trend reversal.
This distinction matters because accumulation phases often test investors’ patience. Prices can remain weak before a stronger move begins.
The biggest takeaway isn’t that Ethereum will immediately rally.
It’s that on-chain fundamentals are quietly improving while sentiment remains cautious. History has shown that these conditions are often worth watching closely.
The market rewards those who prepare before the crowd arrives—not those who chase after the headlines.

I recommend that everyone return to leading crypto assets. There’s only one reason: 
The only sustainable direction for the entire industry in the future is to restore the value of leading assets.

Over the past few years, the crypto market has gone through massive project bubbles, liquidity being stretched beyond capacity, and a drain on trust. Many assets without real demand, without users, and without cash flow backing are, in essence, just short-term speculation tools.

If the market wants to attract larger-scale capital in the future, it must go back to a small number of true leading assets—those with network effects, technical accumulation, and ecosystem value.

Financial markets are always like this:

After a bubble bursts, not all assets come back. Instead, capital searches again for assets that are truly valuable.

The next stage of competition in the crypto industry isn’t about “who issues more tokens,” but about who can become part of the global digital finance infrastructure.

In the 2023–2024 bull market, the industry’s leading narratives—Ordi, PePe, WLD, Sui, ONDO—can’t be said that I was the absolute earliest advocate, but I was the first person to bring up the entire narrative package. Now talking about these is like bragging. But when I wrote the whole narrative framework back when everyone was still thinking about the big pie at thirty thousand, many people also came across me because of those tokens.

Back then, when I went to talk about them, these projects were all at the bottom of the cycle. People even commented that I was writing a novel and “don’t dream in the daytime.” Later, they still ended up getting hyped up because of traffic, heat, and being traded.

At this stage, these kinds of assets are rather boring. In a mature industry, they wouldn’t be well received. But the industry is precisely stepping into a mature phase.

Changing your mindset is a good thing. No matter how the main forces struggle, the whole industry is moving onto a new path of maturity. Whoever stays away from the track will be left behind by the times.

Five years from now, looking back at this post, I realized that I had once also seen—amid the brokenness—a kind of industry that exuded rules, order, vitality, and maturity.

I often chat with friends. In any market, everything follows the laws of the universe: childhood, youth, maturity, aging—and crypto is the same. Right now we’re in the rebellious teenage phase.

If you’re smart enough, and six months ago you were talking about these frameworks, then today when you see leading assets like UNI, SKY, and others, and they can still exude vitality in a market like this, you should be able to roughly estimate their future—and even the overall future framework of the entire industry.

我推荐大家回归加密头部资产，理由只有一个：
整个行业未来唯一可持续的方向，就是修复头部资产的价值。

过去几年，加密市场经历了大量项目泡沫、流动性透支和信任消耗。大量没有真实需求、没有用户、没有现金流支撑的资产，本质上只是短期投机工具。

未来市场想要吸引更大规模资金进入，必须重新回到少数真正具有网络效应、技术积累和生态价值的头部资产。

金融市场永远如此：

泡沫破裂后，不是所有资产都会回来，而是资金重新寻找真正有价值的资产。

加密行业下一阶段的竞争，不是“谁发行更多代币”，而是谁能够成为全球数字金融基础设施的一部分。

2023～2024年牛市，行业头部叙事Ordi、PePe、WLD、Sui、ONDO，不能说我属于百分百最早的提倡者，但我最早提起整段叙事的人。现在讲这些和吹牛一样，但从大饼三万都写下整个叙事框架，很多人也是因为这些代币关注我。

当年去讲他们时，这些项目都在谷底。当时有评论说我在写小说、白天不要做梦之类的话，后来他们还是因为流量、热度、炒了起来。

现在的阶段这类资产很无趣，在一个成熟的行业，都不会受到欢迎，而行业刚好正在步入一个成熟期。

转变一下思维是好事情，无论主力如何挣扎整个行业在步入一个新的成熟轨道，谁远离轨道，谁被时代抛弃。

五年后，回过头看这篇帖子，原来曾经自己也在破碎中看到过一个散发着规则、秩序、生机、成熟的行业。

我经常和朋友聊天，任何市场都遵循着宇宙法则、儿童、青年、成熟、衰老，加密也一样，现在处于青少年叛逆期。

如果你足够聪明，半年前讲这些框架，你今天看到UNI、SKY等头部资产，在这样的市场里还能散发活力，应该可以大概估算他们的未来，乃至整个行业的未来框架。

When you see another “storage-style” collapse in the future, don’t rush in and take the blow.

Many industry sell-offs are not the market mistakenly underpricing companies; they’re a repricing of value after a cyclical reversal.

During periods of high business momentum, capital grants companies unlimited room for imagination. But when supply and demand flip, profits decline, and capital expenditures shrink, valuations may need several years to be digested.

Catching a ride partway up the hill, it may look cheap—but it could end up turning into a wait that lasts a lifetime.

In the end, human society still returns to the most basic needs: food, drink, housing, transportation, and survival.

The stock market is the same.

No matter how great the story is, it ultimately comes back to cash flow, profitability, and real demand.

Three major macro risks in financial markets have already been faintly triggered: debt that is too high and leverage running out of control—it's just waiting for liquidity to disappear, leading to a slow death...

The pattern that repeated in 2018, again in 2022, and that could be happening right now 

$BTC  doesn’t go up in a straight line after a bear market. It never has.

What it does is much more frustrating for retail and much more predictable for anyone who knows the cycles: it consolidates sideways for months, exhausts the impatient, and when nobody expects it, it starts the next major bullish move.

The recurring fractal:

In 2018, BTC consolidated in a range for about 108 days before starting the recovery. In 2022, the consolidation lasted around 202 days. In both cases, the final breakout was confirmed when the price crossed and consolidated above the key moving average.

2026 is showing the same pattern. Same sideways consolidation. Same sentiment exhaustion. Same retail desperation, convinced that this time it’s different.

The signal that few are watching:

In the two previous cycles, right when BTC hit its local bottom, ETH began outperforming Bitcoin. The ETH/BTC pair showed an aggressive rebound exactly in the initial phase of the bottom formation.

That signal is showing up again right now.

What this means for your strategy:

If the fractal plays out, the current prices of $BTC  and $ETH  could be exactly the accumulation zone that, in previous cycles, turned out to be the best entry for the full cycle. Not the perfect entry, but the one that generated the most returns for those who had the patience to hold.

The sideways volatility you’re seeing isn’t weakness. It’s the market changing hands before the real move begins. Those accumulating during this phase are often the ones who end up best positioned when sentiment turns.

This is not financial advice. Fractals rhyme, but they don’t repeat identically. Always trade with risk management and a clearly defined stop loss.

2026 está mostrando el mismo patrón. Misma consolidación lateral. Mismo agotamiento del sentimiento. Misma desesperación del retail convencido de que esta vez es diferente.

Esa señal está apareciendo de nuevo ahora mismo.

🤫 Here’s a secret from my own secrets...
Before I tell you, you have to forget about the idea of support and resistance first—it drags you down in you.

Imagine you entered a produce shop, and you picked everything you need.
You reached the cashier, and they told you: The total is 350 riyals.
You said: Let me go to the store next door.
Same produce... same quality... but the invoice is 220 riyals.
What would you do?
Of course you’d go to the shop that costs less.
And this is exactly one of the market maker’s secrets.
If they have more than one liquidity pool to choose from, they’ll usually prefer the one with the lower access cost.
But pay attention...
Don’t go thinking that every pool with a low cost will definitely be visited.
A pool is measured in more than one way, and access cost is only one factor.
There are other secrets you need to understand—or you won’t be fooled much.
I personally made mistakes once... and twice... and dozens of times, until I started understanding when a pool gets visited and when it gets ignored.
If you understand this idea, you’ll start reading the market with a different mindset... not the mindset of lines, support, and resistance.
